summary: Romania's Ministry of Foreign Affairs offers scholarships to citizens of non-EU countries for bachelor's, master's and doctoral study at Romanian public universities. The award waives fees, pays a monthly scholarship and funds a place in student housing, and starts with a year learning Romanian.
meta_description: Romania's government scholarship for non-EU students: no fees, a monthly allowance and a dorm place, with no age limit. Documents, dates and the language year.
covers: No registration, tuition or other fees, for the standard length of the programme.
A preparatory year of Romanian language, also fee-free.
A monthly scholarship during the preparatory year and the degree.
Accommodation in student dormitories, within the available places and the allocated subsidy.
eligibility: Citizens of non-EU countries. People of Romanian origin, those with protection status in Romania, diplomatic staff and international-organisation staff based in Romania are excluded.
An average of at least 7 out of 10 (or 'Good') in your most recent completed studies.
Bachelor's and master's study is in Romanian only; doctoral study may be in Romanian or another language the doctoral school uses.
Medicine, dental medicine and pharmacy are not available through this scholarship.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Study in Romania scholarships portal (scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro).
Upload the required documents during the application period; for 2026/27 it ran from 16 February to 31 March 2026.
Choose your preferred programmes and universities in the form.
Results are published around mid-July; successful candidates then arrange their visa and start the preparatory year in the autumn.
watch_out: Plan for five years for a bachelor's degree (one preparatory year plus four years of study) unless you can prove Romanian at B1 or previous study in Romanian.
Programmes are taught in Romanian, so commit fully to the language year; you will study your degree in it.
The official pages do not publish the monthly amount, so ask through the portal's contact form before relying on it for living costs.
You can send only one application per call, and it cannot be edited or added to after you submit it. Check every document first.

documents: Diplomas and transcripts from your previous studies, with authorised translations where needed, apostilled under the Hague Convention or otherwise authenticated.
Your birth certificate and the first three pages of a valid passport; you cannot apply without one.
A CV in English, French or Romanian.
For a PhD: a letter of intent and your prospective supervisor's agreement.

Where they apply: proof of a name change, a certificate for exams still pending, a Romanian language certificate at B1 or above (to skip the preparatory year), and parental consent if you are under 18.
Once selected: a medical certificate confirming you are fit to study.

faq.q: Is there an age limit for the Romanian Government scholarship?
faq.a: No. The official FAQ says there is no age limit to apply. You do need an average of at least 7 out of 10, or 'Good', in your most recently completed studies.

Not at bachelor's or master's level: those programmes are taught only in Romanian, after a fee-free preparatory year of Romanian unless you hold a B1 certificate or pass the Romanian test. Doctoral schools may teach in another language.

The 2027/28 call has not been published. For 2026/27, applications ran from 16 February to 31 March 2026 on the Study in Romania platform, the only accepted route, and results were emailed around 15 July 2026.

faq.q: Can I defer the scholarship to a later year?
faq.a: No. It cannot be suspended or transferred to the next academic year. Applicants who already hold a Romanian state scholarship for the same study cycle are excluded, and medicine, dental medicine and pharmacy are not offered.
